clue.text: Money going on the house wine

tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: Someone spends their cash on the house red at a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambertin is a celebrated red Burgundy from Gevrey-Chambertin.

clue.text: Jersey and Guernsey, say, as place for yachting

indicators.note: say signals that the cattle word is only spoken, its sound giving the entry

parts.note: Jersey and Guernsey are breeds of dairy cattle

explanation.surface: The Channel Islands are being offered as a sailing destination.
explanation.walkthrough: Jersey and Guernsey look like the islands, but they are cattle breeds. Cowes, on the Isle of Wight, hosts the famous Cowes Week regatta.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowes is an English port town renowned for its annual sailing regatta.

clue.text: Record-holder accomplished 7 changes

parts.note: arch can mean consummate or skilled, as in an arch exponent

indicators.note: changes tells us the letters of the cross-referenced answer are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to clue 7 down, VISIT

explanation.surface: A skilled champion alters clue seven.
explanation.walkthrough: '7' points to the answer of clue 7 down, whose letters 'changes' rearranges; 'accomplished' is used in its sense of thoroughgoing, as in an arch rogue.
explanation.definitionFit: An archivist keeps and looks after records, so is literally a keeper of documents.

clue.text: Coward's work shortened fight

parts.note: brief means short or cut down
an encounter is a clash or battle

explanation.surface: A timid person's job cut short a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coward' is Noel Coward, the English playwright, not a timid person; Brief Encounter is the 1945 film from his play.
explanation.definitionFit: Brief Encounter was written by Noel Coward, adapted from his one-act play Still Life.

clue.text: University's books

explanation.surface: A college owns some volumes.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading is an English town with a university; reading also means literature or books to read.

clue.text: Disinclination to move, in time, is holding it up

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: is holding means the time word contains the next piece

parts.note: an era is a period of time

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word it is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone reluctant to get going is delaying things just in time.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' means reading upward; 'is holding' looks like part of the surface sense of delaying but signals one piece going inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is the physics term for a body's tendency to resist any change in motion, hence sluggishness.

clue.text: Poet's verse one inserted in unfinished poem

indicators.note: inserted in means the verse and one letters go inside the shortened poem
unfinished means the poem word loses its last letter

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A writer's stanza is slotted into an incomplete poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' cuts ODE to OD; 'inserted in' puts VI inside it. The 's after Poet stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovid was the Roman poet who wrote the Metamorphoses.

clue.text: Attack German weapon on unfinished site

parts.note: the V1 flying bomb of the Second World War, written VI

indicators.note: unfinished means the site word loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before the cut

explanation.surface: A wartime German bomb strikes a half-built site.
explanation.walkthrough: The V1 was the German flying bomb of 1944, often printed V-I; 'unfinished' removes the last letter of the place word.
explanation.definitionFit: To visit can mean to afflict or inflict punishment upon, as a plague is visited on a city.

clue.text: Finding modern type of musical entertainment jolly

parts.note: a disco is a dance venue playing recorded pop music
jolly is British slang for very, as in jolly good

explanation.surface: A new style of show music is great fun.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English, 'jolly' as an adverb means very.
explanation.definitionFit: A discovery is a find, something newly found.

clue.text: The English play

explanation.surface: A nation is described as a drama.
explanation.walkthrough: John of Gaunt in Shakespeare's Richard II calls the English 'this happy breed of men'; Noel Coward borrowed the phrase for his 1939 play.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's phrase describes the English people, and it is also the title of a Coward stage drama.

clue.text: US city getting mad with CIA

indicators.note: getting mad suggests the letters going wild and rearranging

explanation.surface: An American town grows furious with the intelligence agency.
explanation.definitionFit: Wichita is the largest city in Kansas.

clue.text: She gets involved with Sue and Penny, in place of Diana

indicators.note: gets involved means the letters are tangled together and reordered

explanation.surface: A woman mixes with two friends called Sue and Penny where Diana lived.
explanation.walkthrough: Diana is the Roman goddess, not a princess: her great temple (as Artemis) stood at Ephesus.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephesus held the Temple of Artemis, the Greek counterpart of the Roman goddess Diana.

clue.text: He'll give nothing away and hide pirate

parts.note: a hide is an animal's skin
Captain Flint is the pirate in Treasure Island

explanation.surface: A tight-lipped man helps conceal a buccaneer.
explanation.definitionFit: A skinflint is a miser who refuses to part with money.

clue.text: Start fighting round roadblock initially

indicators.note: initially places the roadblock word first, ahead of the round letter

parts.note: a sett is a stone paving block used for roads
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Violence breaks out around a police barricade at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roadblock' is not a barrier but a block for a road: a sett, a granite paving stone.
explanation.definitionFit: To set to is to begin something vigorously, especially a fight.

clue.text: It's an offence, pinching article of Continental type

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, here A

indicators.note: pinching means the offence word grips the article inside it

parts.note: a sin is a moral offence
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Stealing a newspaper piece of a European kind is a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinching' looks like stealing but means holding: A goes inside SIN to make SAIN, after A from 'an'.
explanation.definitionFit: Asian describes someone or something from the continent of Asia.

clue.text: Plant experts introducing Rus sian boy to skills

indicators.note: introducing one thing to another here means putting it inside

parts.note: arts are skills or crafts
Boris is a typical Russian man's name

explanation.surface: Gardeners teach a young Russian their crafts.
explanation.walkthrough: The page splits 'Russian' across a line break.
explanation.definitionFit: Arborists are specialists in the care of trees.

clue.text: Recipient of money holds gold back as security

indicators.note: holds means the recipient word contains the next piece

parts.note: a grantee receives a grant

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.walkthrough: 'Recipient of money' is a one-word synonym for someone given a grant; 'back' reverses the chemical symbol before 'holds' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A guarantee is a pledge or surety given as assurance.

clue.text: Tragedy's beginning, in fact, in a touching way

indicators.note: beginning picks the opening letter of the word for a tragedy

parts.note: actually means in fact or really

explanation.surface: The start of a sad drama is, in truth, moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touching' looks emotional but means relating to touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactually means by way of the sense of touch.

clue.text: Get weaver to drink a toast

parts.note: Bottom is the weaver in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Encourage a cloth-maker to raise a glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weaver' is not a trade here but Nick Bottom from A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottoms up is a cheerful salutation said before draining a glass.

clue.text: Two-thirds of orchestra confused about unknown piece of music

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go round the next piece
confused means those letters are jumbled

explanation.walkthrough: 'Two-thirds of' gives ORCHES, which 'confused' turns into SCHERO; 'about' puts Z inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A scherzo is a lively movement in a symphony or sonata.

clue.text: A despot corrupted magistrate in Italy

indicators.note: corrupted means the letters are spoiled and rearranged

explanation.surface: A tyrant has bribed an Italian official.
explanation.definitionFit: A podesta was the chief magistrate of a medieval Italian city.

clue.text: At one time, you beat retreat fast

to cap is to beat or outdo

explanation.surface: Long ago, you beat a hasty withdrawal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' turns YECAP round to give PACEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Pacey, also spelled pacy, means quick or speedy.

clue.text: Tree sparrow a naturalist shelters

indicators.note: shelters means the words hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher protects a sparrow in a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The rowan, or mountain ash, has red berries.

clue.text: Hazard to shipping requires one to take care in sound

indicators.note: in sound means the word is heard rather than seen

parts.note: to reck is an old word for to heed or care

explanation.surface: Danger to vessels demands caution in a strait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like a stretch of sea, but signals a spoken word.
explanation.definitionFit: A wreck is a sunken or stranded vessel that endangers navigation.

clue.text: Doctor's alter ego, say, certain to be narrow-minded

bound means sure, as in bound to happen

explanation.surface: Jekyll's dark side is sure to be bigoted.
explanation.definitionFit: Hidebound means rigidly conventional and closed to new ideas.

clue.text: Trick had briefly taken in the Venetian official

indicators.note: taken in means the short form goes inside the official

parts.note: the doge was the elected ruler of Venice
had shortened to 'd, as in I'd

explanation.surface: A Venetian ruler was briefly deceived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' suggests being fooled, but puts D inside DOGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodge is a cunning ruse or scheme.

clue.text: Novel transport for deadlier female

parts.note: She is H. Rider Haggard's novel
to bear is to carry

explanation.surface: A book is exchanged for a more dangerous woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling wrote that the female of the species is more deadly than the male, beginning with the she-bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling's poem cites the female bear as fiercer than its mate.

clue.text: Deprived of protective cover, subjected to bombardment

explanation.surface: Troops are stripped of cover under artillery fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Shelled means with its husk or pod removed, and also attacked by artillery fire.

clue.text: Interest in drink

explanation.surface: Someone is keen on a beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: For the sake of means in the interest of; sake is Japanese rice wine.

clue.text: His consultant and medical assistant became famous

definitions.text: His consultant and medical assistant became famous

parts.words: His consultant and medical assistant became famous
parts.note: the consulting detective and his doctor sidekick made the creator of the Baker Street tales world-famous
